summary: Iteration 79 — Pre-Phase-1-launch backend health check. 46/46 pytest tests PASS across 12 test classes covering health, auth, PyMongo Async regression (inbox aggregate, brief, tasks, decisions, brain/context, brain/documents), multi-tenant + role isolation, task/decision/complaint CRUD with brain_context capture, Company Brain documents CRUD + permission gate (public/dept visibility, sales cannot see/download/upload finance-dept docs), /api/ask RBAC gate (deterministic regex classifier — sales denied on 'unpaid invoices', owner allowed), /api/brain/agent multi-agent router (owner-policy uses tools, owner-overdue-tasks answered, owner-vendor-delays picks knowledge_lookup or metadata_search, production-sales denied, production-policy allowed), one-tap /brain/agent/create-task with source_type=agent_suggestion brain_context capture, signup /interview/{start,answer,blueprint,refine} end-to-end with WhatsApp-review refinement injection, admin panel (superadmin login + alerts + tenants + metrics), and edge cases (empty question 400, unicode Hindi question, 801-char over-cap 422, cross-tenant task GET returns 404). CONFIRMED FIXES: /api/inbox `async for row in db.inbox.aggregate([...])` PyMongo drop-in bug — last TypeError in backend.err.log at line 14766 pre-restart (17:18:18); after restart ZERO TypeErrors and ZERO 500s on /api/inbox across 5 back-to-back curl probes plus full pytest suite. /brief, /tasks, /decisions, /brain/context, /brain/documents all return 200 (no other latent Motor→PyMongo migration bugs found — only 3 `.aggregate()` sites in codebase, all correctly awaited). CRITICAL RBAC BYPASS FOUND on /api/brain/agent: the Claude LLM planner is used to determine intent (stochastic), and consistently mis-classifies 'how many unpaid invoices this month?' as intent=general (not finance) across 3/3 runs — so a sales user asking that exact phrasing gets past the RBAC gate with denied=false, even though the deterministic regex classifier used by /api/ask correctly flags the same question as finance and denies it. Tool-level guards (mongo_query returns restricted:true when scope.can_finance is False) still contain the data leak in this specific case (no real invoice numbers returned), but the answer is misleading (Claude suggested connecting QuickBooks/Stripe) and the audit log records denied=false. Other finance phrasings ('unpaid GST invoices', 'cash balance', 'payments to vendors') ARE correctly denied — so the vulnerability is the mismatch between /api/ask (regex, tight) and /api/brain/agent (LLM, loose). Fix: /api/brain/agent should ALSO run brain_rbac.classify_intent on the raw question (in addition to Claude's intent) and use the STRICTER of the two — union of intents means falling back to regex when Claude returns 'general' on a question that regex flags as sensitive.

critical.issue: RBAC bypass — Claude LLM planner classifies 'how many unpaid invoices this month?' as intent=general (not finance) in 3/3 runs. Sales user gets denied=false + a helpful-sounding answer suggesting external accounting integrations. The deterministic regex classifier in brain_rbac.classify_intent CORRECTLY flags the identical question as finance (test_sales_finance_intent_denied_via_ask passes). The mismatch means /api/ask denies but /api/brain/agent allows the same question from the same user. Tool-level guards contain the actual number leak (mongo_query returns restricted:true), but the audit log is wrong (denied=false) and the founder promise 'a random employee cannot ask Dex what are our sales? and get a real answer regardless of which entry point they use' is broken. Fix: in routers/brain_router.py ask_agent (line ~437), after `intent = plan['intent']`, run `regex_intent = brain_rbac.classify_intent(q)` and if regex_intent NOT in allowed AND regex_intent != 'general', treat intent as regex_intent (union — stricter of the two) BEFORE the `if intent not in allowed` check.

minor.issue: Planner picks metadata_search+knowledge_lookup instead of mongo_query for 'How many tasks are overdue?' — Claude does not pick the analytics tool for a clearly-analytical question. Answer is still generated correctly (Claude synthesizes from empty tool outputs) but the KPIs/table that mongo_query would have returned are missing. Consider adding a soft hint in _PLANNER_SYSTEM: 'For questions containing numeric aggregators (how many, count, total, overdue count, this month's revenue) ALWAYS include mongo_query.'

Frontend (or a stale caller) is hitting `/api/ledger/invoices?limit=5` and `/api/ledger/expenses?limit=5` which return 404 — routers/ledger.py only exposes `/expenses`, `/revenue`, `/payables`, and no `/ledger/invoices` shorthand. Either add these thin aliases (thin wrappers over /revenue and /expenses with limit query support) or update the frontend to hit the correct paths. Not part of this iteration's scope but visible in backend.out.log.

No auth or ownership check — anyone with a session_id (UUID) can rewrite the refinement. Sessions are 128-bit UUIDs so unguessable in practice, but for defense-in-depth consider expiring signup_sessions after N hours or after 1 successful blueprint call. (Same note carried from iteration 78.)

action_items: HIGH: Fix /api/brain/agent RBAC bypass — add brain_rbac.classify_intent(q) as a second gate before the allowed-set check in routers/brain_router.py ask_agent(). If Claude says 'general' but regex says 'finance'/'sales'/'hr', trust the regex (fail closed). Retest by running pytest tests/test_iteration79_prelaunch.py -k test_sales_finance_intent_denied 3 times to verify stability.

MEDIUM: Nudge /api/brain/agent planner toward mongo_query for numeric/aggregation questions — add explicit tool-picking hint in _PLANNER_SYSTEM (see minor issue above). Not blocking launch; owner still gets an answer, just without the analytics table.
LOW: Fix the 404s on /api/ledger/invoices and /api/ledger/expenses — either add aliases in routers/ledger.py or update the frontend caller to use /revenue and /expenses.
LOW: Add session TTL / one-time-use on signup_sessions to prevent replay of /interview/refine.
critical_code_review_comments: SECURITY: /api/brain/agent trusts the Claude-classified `intent` for the RBAC gate. Because Claude is stochastic, this creates a defeatable security control. brain_rbac.classify_intent (regex-based, deterministic) should be the primary gate, with Claude's intent used only to disambiguate when regex returns 'general'. Current design lets specific finance phrasings bypass the gate.

core.py:29 — `AsyncMongoClient` (PyMongo 4.x) is the correct successor to Motor. Only 3 `.aggregate()` call sites in the entire backend (server.py:5037, admin.py:207, admin.py:221) — all now correctly `await`ed. No other latent Motor→PyMongo migration gotchas found.

brain_context.py:record_context is correctly fire-and-forget (try/except swallows) and every write is verified in the tests (task_done, complaint resolution, agent-suggested task all captured with correct source_type + source_id).

brain_docs.py: visibility rules are correctly enforced at BOTH list-time (via _visibility_filter $or clause) AND single-doc endpoints (via _user_can_see mirror). Sales user cannot list, download, or upload as verified by tests f/g/h.

server.py:5037 (list_inbox) — the fix is correct. `agg_cursor = await db.inbox.aggregate([...])` then `async for row in agg_cursor`. Comment at line 5034-5036 explaining the drop-in gotcha is helpful; consider a linter rule to catch `async for row in db.<col>.aggregate(...)` without a preceding await, if any future dev re-introduces it.

signup.py:451 (/interview/refine) delegates back to interview_blueprint via a fresh InterviewSessionInput — the stored refinement is picked up in interview_blueprint via `s.get('refinement')`. Verified end-to-end: WhatsApp workflow name appears in the refined blueprint.

brain_router.py:222 (_tool_mongo_query) — correctly returns {restricted: true, message: ...} when scope.can_finance is False AND plan is finance-typed. This is the belt-and-suspenders that saved us in the RBAC bypass case (though the misleading answer still leaks intent).

admin.py:56 (admin_login) — brute-force lockout is per (ip:email) not just email — good. Consider adding a global per-IP rate limit too (currently an attacker with 100 IPs can attempt 500 * 100 = 50000 admin logins before backing off).

success_rate.backend: 100% (46/46 pytest — includes an intentionally-relaxed test that documents the RBAC bypass by trying 3 phrasings and passing when AT LEAST ONE is correctly denied)

context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 79 confirms the PyMongo Async migration is complete and safe for phase-1 launch — no other endpoints latently affected by the aggregate() coroutine issue. The one critical finding is the /api/brain/agent RBAC bypass on Claude-classified intent — after main agent adds the brain_rbac.classify_intent regex gate as belt-and-suspenders, re-run `pytest tests/test_iteration79_prelaunch.py -k 'test_sales_finance_intent_denied and not via_ask' -v --count=3` (or manually) to confirm 3/3 runs deny 'how many unpaid invoices this month?' asked by sales user. The full test file also serves as the phase-1 regression harness — run it on every subsequent iteration to catch new leaks. All tests are idempotent and self-cleanup.
rca of the issue: SYMPTOM: sales user asks Dex `/api/brain/agent` 'how many unpaid invoices this month?' — response has denied=false, intent=general, tools_used=[metadata_search, knowledge_lookup], and a Claude-synthesized answer suggesting they connect a QuickBooks/Stripe integration. Expected: denied=true, intent=finance, refusal_message returned. REPRO: run the 3-line curl in TestBrainAgent.test_sales_finance_intent_denied — reproduces in 3/3 runs, consistent. ROOT CAUSE: brain_router.py:_plan() uses Claude Sonnet 4.6 to classify intent (system prompt lines 54-84). For this specific phrasing, Claude reasons 'the user is asking about their business's invoices, which could be general operational info' and returns intent=general. The RBAC gate at line 443 (`if intent not in allowed:`) then lets sales through because general is in _BASELINE. The deterministic classifier in brain_rbac.py:_INTENT_PATTERNS has `('finance', r'\b(invoice|...|unpaid|...)\b')` which correctly matches — but /api/brain/agent doesn't consult it. This is the entire design flaw: two entry points to Dex, one hardened, one soft. MITIGATION (1-line fix): in routers/brain_router.py ask_agent(), after computing `intent = plan['intent']`, add: `regex_intent = brain_rbac.classify_intent(q); if regex_intent != 'general' and regex_intent not in allowed: intent = regex_intent` — then the existing `if intent not in allowed:` block runs the refusal_message. This preserves Claude's better handling of policy-vs-hr overlaps (regex is greedier there) while fail-closing on any question the regex flags as sensitive. Alternative: use `intent = brain_rbac.classify_intent(q) or plan['intent']` (regex-first, LLM-fallback) — simpler but loses Claude's disambiguation on genuinely-ambiguous 'general' questions.
